text:
ashley: FYI customer-tenant-42 wants to push a customer-managed rate policy into their Private VPC (S3 object). Question: how do we validate, preview, and actually enforce without risking outages?
ben: +1 on safety. I think we need a dry-run mode for any customer-provided policy. It should be accepted by control plane, validated, and then passed to dataplane as a ‘candidate’ until promoted.
ciara: we also need signing/verification. If they push to S3 we should require a signed manifest (KMS/HMAC) and validate against a whitelist schema. No unsigned policies in prod.
hazel: UX: Console should show a diff between active policy and candidate, with simulated QPS curves and example requests that would be affected. Dry-run toggle visible with clear "no enforcement" label.
ben: proposed policy JSON example (simple):
```json
{
  "version": "2026-01-01",
  "scope": "org",
  "identifier": "tenant-42-policy-v1",
  "rules": [
    {
      "route": "*",
      "limit": {"per_minute": 60000, "burst": 1200},
      "apply_to": ["api_key","org_id"]
    },
    {
      "route": "/v1/embeddings",
      "limit": {"per_minute": 30000, "burst": 800},
      "priority": 100
    }
  ],
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG_HERE"
}
```
ashley: that looks good. A couple architecture tradeoffs: enforce in control plane (easy to change, slower) vs dataplane (fast, single hop). For Private VPC we already have a local control-plane agent running in the customer subnet — maybe it can validate + push the compiled token-buckets to the local dataplane.
ciara: exactly. Don't let central control-plane be the single enforcement hop for latency-sensitive requests. Validation and audit can be central, but enforcement should be local in the VPC. Also require policies to be immutable once promoted (versioned).
hazel: from UX/rollout POV we need: 1) dry-run window (7 days), 2) canary percent (apply to X% of keys), 3) automatic telemetry collection showing "would-have-been" rejects.
ben: telemetry design: include labels: tenant_id, api_key_id, route, enforcement_reason (e.g., global_quota, org_quota, per_key_quota, burst_exceeded), decision (allow/deny/would_deny). Send these to Metrics + a sampled trace to the Console policy preview.
ashley: what about precedence? my suggestion: explicit per-key rules > per-org rules > route-specific > global fallback. If a rule is missing we fallback to the next level. Documented and deterministic.
ciara: need safety nets: a global kill-switch per-region and a conservative global fallback policy for newly onboarded tenants (so misconfigs don't tank nodes). Also require an automatic schema lint that rejects obviously dangerous configs (e.g., limit=0 for all routes).
ben: implementation note: compile policies down to a small set of token-bucket params stored in redis/faststore in dataplane. Candidate/dry-run mode should annotate but not mutate token buckets; we store a parallel simulation counter.
hazel: Console details: show time-series of actual vs simulated rejects, a toggle to "promote" candidate, and a small diff that highlights which API keys will see behavior changes. Add a confirm modal that requires typing the tenant id to prevent accidental promotes.
deploy-bot: [policy-upload] tenant-42 candidate policy uploaded by ashley at 2026-03-18T21:14:49Z :white_check_mark:
ashley: ok action items: (1) ben & eng-runtime implement candidate/promotion API + compile-to-tokenbucket, (2) ciara add signature & schema validation + audited webhook sink, (3) hazel wire up policy-diff UI + dry-run metrics in Console. I'll file tickets. :thumbsup:
ciara: also add an ops playbook: steps to rollback promoted policy and a runtime inspector endpoint to show effective policy for a given api_key.
ben: final note: consider an automated canary rollouts feature: promote to 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automated health checks (latency, error-rate, regressions) before full promotion. lowers blast radius.
ashley: agreed. let's sync on implementation plan in tomorrow's platform sync. Thanks all.
